claims.text: Gas-atomized AlCrFeNiSi powder is suitable as feedstock for laser additive manufacturing.
The intervention is active cryogenic substrate cooling during laser deposition, with the substrate maintained near -150°C.
Cryogenic substrate cooling moderates the thermal input experienced by the deposited material.
The cooled substrate absorbs excess thermal energy from the melt pool.
Cryogenic substrate cooling lowers peak thermal gradients during solidification.
Cryogenic substrate cooling minimizes rapid temperature fluctuations and controls solidification rates.
The altered thermal history produces a refined and more homogeneous microstructure.
The cryogenically processed microstructure contains fewer dislocations.
Cryogenic substrate cooling reduces internal and residual thermal stresses relative to conventional high-thermal-load processing.
Cryogenically cooled AlCrFeNiSi components have higher yield strength than conventionally processed components.
Cryogenically cooled AlCrFeNiSi components have greater ductility than conventionally processed components.
Cryogenic substrate cooling reduces the need for complex post-build treatments and thereby simplifies the processing workflow.
Conventional high-energy laser additive manufacturing of AlCrFeNiSi produces steep thermal gradients, residual stresses, and degraded mechanical properties.
The proposed process is applicable primarily to miniature components with characteristic features below 5 mm.
Larger geometries or cooling temperatures outside the proposed window may fail to provide the same benefits and may introduce defects.
Cryogenic processing may produce secondary changes in phase evolution.
